corrected_answer:
Analytical stance under test: Stance 100 - Interconnect discovery must precede the layout choice, because the transport NCCL actually selects, not the one on the datasheet, sets the collective floor.

Common frame (applies to every stance below).
Assumptions (must be restated by the answering engineer, not inherited silently):
A1. Single node, 8 GPUs, NVLink/NVSwitch intra-node; inter-node paths only appear where a stance says so explicitly.
A2. Decode-dominant, latency-sensitive serving: the SLO is TTFT p95 and TPOT (inter-token latency) p95, never a mean.
A3. Model weights fit in aggregate HBM with at least 20% KV-cache headroom at target concurrency.
A4. Exactly one variable moves per arm: no simultaneous change of quantization, batching policy, or speculative decoding.
Mechanism, stated plainly:
- Tensor parallelism (TP) shards every layer's GEMMs. Each transformer block needs two all-reduces (after attention out-projection and after the MLP down-projection), so decode carries L * 2 * allreduce_latency of synchronous cost, where L is the layer count. TP is latency-additive in collectives but capacity- and bandwidth-multiplying: per-GPU weight bytes and per-GPU KV bytes both fall by the TP degree.
- Pipeline parallelism (PP) shards layers into stages. Per token it adds only (PP-1) small point-to-point hidden-state sends, which are cheap, but a single request serializes through all stages and the bubble fraction is (PP-1)/(micro_batches + PP-1). At low concurrency there are too few in-flight micro-batches to fill the pipeline, so PP loses badly on single-request latency.
Boundary conditions that flip the answer:
- B1. On NVLink-class fabric, small-message all-reduce latency is in the single-digit microseconds and TP up to 8 is normally latency-viable. Over PCIe-only or across nodes on RoCE/IB the same collective's latency floor rises roughly an order of magnitude and TP stops paying past TP=2 (ESTIMATE; derivation: decode all-reduce payload is hidden_size * dtype_bytes per token per layer, which is small, so the collective is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound and the per-hop latency floor dominates).
- B2. If the model cannot fit on one GPU, sharding is mandatory and the question reduces to which axis, not whether.
- B3. Under high, steady concurrency the PP bubble amortizes and PP becomes competitive on throughput per GPU while still losing on single-request latency.
Default recommendation: use TP inside the node up to the point where collective cost stops being repaid by reduced per-GPU memory traffic; use PP only to cross a node boundary or to fit a model TP alone cannot fit. PP is not a latency optimization.

Only values read out of named benchmark artifacts may be labelled MEASURED. This review reports no MEASURED values, because no benchmark was executed for it.

The comparison is undecidable until the realised transport is known. NCCL picks a path per communicator - NVLink/NVSwitch, PCIe P2P, shared-memory staging, or a network transport - and a silent fallback to shared memory or PCIe turns a microsecond-class all-reduce into a tens-of-microseconds one, multiplied by two collectives per layer per token. That single misconfiguration is large enough to make tensor parallelism look intrinsically bad when the fabric, not the layout, is at fault. Falsifiable hypothesis H100: forcing NCCL onto the PCIe/shared-memory path while holding model, traffic and tensor degree fixed will raise decode TPOT p95 by a factor far larger than any difference between the tensor and pipeline arms measured on the healthy fabric (ESTIMATE; derivation: decode adds 2*L latency-bound collectives per token, so a per-collective latency floor that rises an order of magnitude scales the whole synchronous term by that order, whereas the layout choice only re-partitions it). Controlled experiment: Capture NCCL_DEBUG=INFO transport-selection output for the healthy topology, then re-run the identical workload with the fast path disabled by environment variable only, changing nothing else. Compare TPOT p95 across the two, then re-run the tensor-versus-pipeline comparison on the healthy fabric alone. Rollback gate: revert to the previously validated layout if the canary's TTFT p95, TPOT p95 or error rate breaches the pre-declared bound, regardless of any aggregate throughput gain observed.

Per-token KV bytes are 2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * dtype_bytes, and the resident KV set is that times sequence length times concurrency. Tensor parallelism shards KV across ranks and so relieves this directly; pipeline parallelism splits it by layer, which relieves it too but leaves each stage holding full-width KV for its own layers. A comparison run at short context can therefore rank the layouts one way and invert once production traffic carries long prompts. Falsifiable hypothesis H101: the tensor and pipeline arms will rank differently at short and long context, and the crossover point is the sequence length at which the per-device KV working set of the weaker arm exceeds its remaining HBM headroom (ESTIMATE; derivation: resident KV scales linearly in sequence length and concurrency while device capacity is fixed, so the feasible-degree constraint binds at a computable length). Controlled experiment: Hold model, engine, tensor degree and pipeline degree fixed and sweep only the input-length distribution across at least four buckets spanning the production percentiles. Record per-device KV bytes, preemption and cache-eviction counts, and TTFT/TPOT p95 per bucket for both arms. Rollback gate: revert to the previously validated layout if the canary's TTFT p95, TPOT p95 or error rate breaches the pre-declared bound, regardless of any aggregate throughput gain observed.

Tensor parallelism partitions attention by heads and the MLP by hidden dimension. If the key-value head count under grouped-query attention is smaller than the tensor degree, the engine must either replicate KV heads across ranks - which destroys the expected per-device KV saving - or refuse the configuration. The memory argument that motivated the higher degree can therefore evaporate exactly at the degree where it was needed. Falsifiable hypothesis H102: raising the tensor degree above the number of key-value heads will not reduce per-device KV bytes proportionally, and the measured per-device KV occupancy will flatten at that boundary instead of continuing to fall (ESTIMATE; derivation: KV sharding is along the key-value head axis, so once the degree exceeds that head count the remaining ranks must hold replicated copies). Controlled experiment: Sweep the tensor degree across the divisors of the head and key-value-head counts, including one degree above the key-value head count if the engine permits it, holding model and traffic fixed. Read per-device KV bytes directly from the engine rather than inferring them from free memory. Rollback gate: revert to the previously validated layout if the canary's TTFT p95, TPOT p95 or error rate breaches the pre-declared bound, regardless of any aggregate throughput gain observed.

The naive fill-drain schedule leaves a bubble of (PP-1)/(micro_batches + PP-1); interleaved and one-forward-one-backward style schedules cut that at the cost of more activation residency and more frequent stage-to-stage sends. Reporting a pipeline arm without naming its schedule and in-flight depth makes the number unreproducible. Rollback gate: revert to the previously validated layout if the canary's TTFT p95, TPOT p95 or error rate breaches the pre-declared bound, regardless of any aggregate throughput gain observed.
